speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the history of no prenatal care, unavailable immunization records, and normal blood work so far, I need to assess for signs of congenital syphilis or tuberculosis. Does the baby have a rash, specifically on the palms or soles, or any nasal discharge resembling a "snuffles"? Also, do you notice any bone pain, hepatosplenomegaly, or a failure to thrive?

REQUEST TEST: VDRL
REQUEST TEST: TST_Skin_Test

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Syphilis

The history of no prenatal care and unavailable immunization records raises a high suspicion for congenital syphilis, even though the CBC and Culture were normal (which is common in early neonatal presentation). The VDRL and TST results are pending, but clinically I am most concerned about syphilitic manifestations like a maculopapular rash on the palms and soles, "snuffles" (nasal discharge), or hepatosplenomegaly.

REQUEST IMAGES: Please return photos of the skin, specifically focusing on the palms and soles, to look for a pathognomonic rash.
